solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fox burying head in mound

indicators.note: to bury the head is to hide the first letter away, so the opening letter of the word disappears

parts.note: to fox or stump someone is to baffle them

explanation.surface: A fox digging its head into a mound, as if hiding or hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' is a verb here, not the animal: STUMP loses its head S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tump is a dialect word for a small hillock or heap of earth.

clue.text: Bandage that's elastic I put round large end of oxter

indicators.note: round says the stretched letters go around another word
elastic means stretchy and pliable, so the letters are bent into a new shape
the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the last letter of oxter, a Scots word for armpit

explanation.surface: Someone applies an elastic bandage around their armpit.
explanation.walkthrough: An oxter is the armpit in Scots and northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubigrip is a trade name for a tubular elastic support bandage.

clue.text: Soldier joining revolutionary group of vassals

parts.note: a man is a soldier, as in officers and men
a Red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A soldier signs up with a band of revolutionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Manred is an old word for homage, and by extension a body of vassals owing it to a lord.

clue.text: Spithead has berth for this core section

indicators.note: a berth is a place to lie inside, so the place name holds the word within it

explanation.surface: Spithead, the naval anchorage off Portsmouth, offers a mooring for this central part.
explanation.walkthrough: Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth used as a naval anchorage, which suits the berth.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the soft central tissue of a plant stem, so the core or central part.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well who gets heroin, bypassing a rule

indicators.note: the outer word goes round, passing by on both sides of the inner pair of words

explanation.surface: A wastrel scores drugs while ignoring the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Scag is drug slang for heroin; the rule plus A is wrapped by it rather than tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalawag (scallywag) is a rascal, a good-for-nothing scamp.

clue.text: Skull-cap: each strangely is inscribed with something like an X

indicators.note: inscribed means written inside, so one piece is placed within the other
strangely means oddly, so the letters are set out in an odd order

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like an X

explanation.surface: Each skull-cap is oddly marked with a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A chechia is a close-fitting cylindrical cap worn in North Africa, a kind of skullcap.

clue.text: Object, getting fit, runs included

indicators.note: included means taken inside, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman protests at having a fit, with runs counted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to raise objections, to disagree.

clue.text: I support inland revenue going into fiction bookselling

indicators.note: going into places the earlier parts inside the following word

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
IR abbreviates Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: A bookseller backing the taxman getting into fiction publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Librairie is French for bookshop and the book trade, used in English for bookselling.

clue.text: N. American deer making a den in Wisconsin

indicators.note: in places the den inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WI is the US postal code for Wisconsin
a pit can be an animal's den

explanation.surface: A deer bedding down in a den in Wisconsin.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American elk, a species of deer.

clue.text: Intercommunicate, like cat with a scent around

indicators.note: around says the second phrase wraps about the first

parts.note: the nose of a wine is its scent
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Animals communicating like a cat that sniffs around a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: To anastomose is for vessels or channels to join and open into one another, so to interconnect.

clue.text: Rude fellow annoyed husband

parts.note: something that annoys you gets you, so annoyed is got

explanation.surface: A boorish man irritated her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'annoyed' is the verb, past tense: it got (to) him.
explanation.definitionFit: A Goth, from the barbarian tribe, is a rude, uncivilised person.

clue.text: Pastor with peculiar haircut I noted at the sides, and nothing on top!

definitions.text: at the sides, and nothing on top!

indicators.note: a peculiar haircut is an odd one, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for pastor

explanation.surface: A balding pastor's odd hairstyle: hair at the sides, none on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface describes a bald man's haircut, but the definition describes a building with walls and no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Upaithric describes a temple or building that is roofless, open to the sky above its walls.

clue.text: Language group current in Bhutan (not hard)

indicators.note: current suggests flowing, fluid letters that run into a new order
'not' tells us to drop the letter standing for hard from the word

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard; it is removed

explanation.surface: Which languages are spoken in Bhutan, apart from the harsh ones?
explanation.walkthrough: Bhutan without its H is rearranged into BANTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is the large family of related languages spoken across central and southern Africa.

clue.text: A geek coming up interrupts a row? It raises one's blood pressure

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something
in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top

explanation.surface: A nerd stands up to interrupt a quarrel, which gets one's blood boiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of things. The reversal takes in the first A too.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released under stress that raises heart rate and blood pressure.

clue.text: Vamp's covering minor quarrel, and felt furious

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gaiter covering the vamp, the upper front of a shoe
third meaning: past tense of spit, to be in a rage

explanation.surface: A seductress gets into a little row and is livid.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions, not two. 'Vamp' looks like a femme fatale but is the upper of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaiter over the shoe, a tiff, and the past tense of spit (to fume with anger) all share one spelling.

clue.text: Recollection, as in names recollected

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected means gathered up again in a different order

explanation.surface: Memory, as when names come back to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and indicator echo each other: the anagram signal is also a synonym of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anamnesis is the act of recalling to memory, reminiscence.

clue.text: Spicy food, hot and not English — detestable?

indicators.note: 'not' asks for the letter standing for English to be left out of the dish

parts.note: E abbreviates English; it is dropped
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Is fiery foreign food, hot and un-English, to be despised?
explanation.definitionFit: Currish means like a cur, a mongrel dog, hence mean, snarling and contemptible.

clue.text: One of the hardwood trees, the genera wild rook nests in

indicators.note: a bird nests inside something, so the rook's letter goes inside the other letters
wild means untamed and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a fresh order

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook nesting among various kinds of hardwood tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenheart is a South American tree whose very hard timber is used for piers and boats.

clue.text: Without last rites due possibly when Granny L's interred

indicators.note: interred means buried, so the other letters are laid inside
possibly means in some possible form, so the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: EL is the letter L spelt out

explanation.surface: Granny is buried without the last rites she was owed.
explanation.walkthrough: Unaneled is Hamlet's word: his father's ghost died unhouseled, disappointed, unaneled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaneled means not having received extreme unction, the anointing given before death.

clue.text: Embarrassed by over, have a second try

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A bowler embarrassed by a bad over wants another go.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to do it again, making another attempt.

clue.text: Royal favourite in power cutting do

indicators.note: cutting means slicing off, so the named letters are trimmed away from the word

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are cut away

explanation.surface: A king's favourite, in power, slashing the budget for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party but is just the two letters cut from DOMINION.
explanation.definitionFit: A minion was historically a servile favourite of a monarch, a fawning dependant.

clue.text: Small winding rope in the sea, short length thrown in

indicators.note: thrown in says the letter is tossed inside the other word

parts.note: marine means of or in the sea
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A short rope is thrown into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Marline is a light two-strand rope or cord used on ships for binding.

clue.text: Mixed martini, not right for covering of blood vessel?

indicators.note: a mixed cocktail is shaken up, so its letters are stirred into a new order
'not' instructs leaving out the letter that stands for right

parts.note: R abbreviates right; it is removed

explanation.surface: A cocktail mixed wrongly as a remedy for the blood vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: The intima is the innermost lining layer of an artery or vein.

clue.text: Plain cotton for India, quantity in swatch half rejected

indicators.note: in places the quantity inside what remains
half of the word is thrown out, leaving only the other half

parts.note: taken as written; its first half is dropped

explanation.surface: A sample of plain Indian cotton, half of it sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: T-cloth was a plain cotton fabric made for the Indian market, stamped with a T.

clue.text: The essence of Italy, Latin penned by a master

indicators.note: what is penned by someone is enclosed as in a pen, so one part sits inside another

explanation.surface: A scholar writes Latin, the very soul of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to an Italian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma is Italian for soul, the essential spirit; 'of Italy' flags the foreign language.

clue.text: What gula reveals? It's not far from it

indicators.note: the word reveals how it is built, read as one letter sitting in the rest

parts.note: GULA can be described as L placed in GUA, and that description spelt out is the entry

explanation.surface: What the gullet shows, and something close by it.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the entry, read as L IN GUA, is the instruction that builds the word gula. 'It' in the definition is the gula, the upper throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingua is Latin for tongue, which lies just by the gula or gullet at the back of the mouth.

clue.text: Ruth in corn, to it appearing alien?

indicators.note: something alien looks strange and unfamiliar, so the letters take on a foreign arrangement

explanation.surface: Ruth, the biblical gleaner, among alien corn, as Keats pictured her.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like the biblical woman in a cornfield, but it is the old noun meaning remorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for sorrow or remorse, the root of ruthless, so a synonym of penitence.

clue.text: Form of divorce? There's gossip about one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word wraps round the single letter

explanation.surface: A divorce, and everyone gossips about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Talak is the Islamic divorce in which a husband repudiates his wife by declaration.

clue.text: Left hour for dipping into a trusty old catholicon?

indicators.note: dipping into something places one thing inside another

parts.note: leal is an old and Scots word for loyal or trusty

explanation.surface: An hour left for trying an old remedy of proven reliability.
explanation.walkthrough: Leal survives mainly in Scots, as in 'the land o' the leal'; 'old' flags it as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Allheal is valerian or similar plants thought to cure everything, and a catholicon is a universal remedy.

clue.text: Pike follows acting typical of seniors in Dad's Army?

definitions.text: typical of seniors in Dad's Army

parts.note: A abbreviates acting, as in a military rank
ged is a Scots word for the pike fish

explanation.surface: Private Pike follows the acting of the old men in Dad's Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a British sitcom about an elderly Home Guard platoon whose youngest member is Private Pike. Here pike is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, as most of the platoon's members were.

clue.text: Care for the old with cold on the chest

parts.note: an ark is a chest or coffer

explanation.surface: Looking after elderly people who have a chesty cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the old' marks the definition as archaic, not a care home. In a down entry, 'on' puts C above ARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Cark is an archaic word for anxiety or burden, worry, which is one sense of care.

clue.text: Orcadian gullies, reverse of steep? I'll plunge in

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start
to plunge in is to go inside, so the single letter sits within the other letters

parts.note: to sog is to soak, as one steeps something
the speaker, I, is the letter that will plunge in

explanation.surface: Steep gullies in Orkney, and someone vowing to dive in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective for gullies, but it is the verb meaning soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A gio or geo is an Orkney and Shetland word for a narrow creek or gully in a cliff.

clue.text: Ball for Andy, set showing one with no games for opponent?

definitions.text: one with no games for opponent?

parts.note: ba' is Scots for ball, as Andy Murray, a Scot, might say
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: Andy Murray serving and winning a set without dropping a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Andy' signals Scots speech; 'set' looks like tennis but means to solidify.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis slang a bagel is a 6-0 set, the zero resembling the ring-shaped bread roll.

clue.text: Very uncivil in RSC, Ian replaces one queen in part of another in play? (9, two words)

indicators.note: replaces says one name takes the place of some letters inside another word

parts.note: Gertrude is the queen in Hamlet, a play the RSC stages
ER is Elizabeth Regina; these letters go out
taken as written; this name goes in

explanation.surface: At the Royal Shakespeare Company, an actor called Ian takes over a queen's role.
explanation.walkthrough: RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company. Giant as an adverb meaning very is Scots and dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant here works as an intensifier like very, and rude means uncivil, so the phrase is very impolite.

clue.text: Shed duke rebuilt, once stripped of outer casing

indicators.note: rebuilt means constructed again, so the letters are put together in another way

explanation.surface: A duke's shed is rebuilt after being stripped to its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehusk grain or nuts is to remove the husk, its protective outer layer.

clue.text: African chief, one clad in leather

indicators.note: clad in means dressed in, so one letter is wrapped inside the material

parts.note: kid is soft leather from a young goat

explanation.surface: A tribal chief dressed in leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaid or caid is a North African chief or governor, a local headman.
